text:
This review is for TIKBABA's portable personal blender. Let me start by saying that I bought this to bring on a cruise ship where smoothies aren't readily available but I don't want the same breakfast buffet day after day. I think this will work great in that type of environment where you have a range of fruit and available milk, ice cream, and small ice cubes to whip something up. The blender is really lightweight and fairly small, and you can use the hot water to rinse it out and reuse it.

Take this to a home's kitchen, and I'm finding it more difficult to justify rather than just a fullsize blender that you can get at a cheaper price at a Walmart or Target. The blender is personal size, but it didn't fill an 8oz cup. You're going to be making several smoothies at a time if you intend for it to make something that compares to any smoothie or juice restaurant. The blades appear to be well made, but it took a lot of use to get them to actually chop up my thicker refrigerator ice. They worked really well on smaller ice cubes---you know, the "good ice" from certain chicken fast food chains. But, my refrigerator ice challenged this blender.

The device came charged so it was easy to use after a quick cleaning. I didn't have to track down batteries or wait for it to charge. The instructions are really simple and a quick read though it's fairly intuitive what you're meant to do with the different components.

title: Works well for most things, appreciate the glass container
text:
[[VIDEOID:c1e5c7b1638bc2bb98b16608433499cf]] This is the first personal size blender I've ever used. It works pretty good.

The Good:
- I like that this personal blender has a glass container versus plastic. - The container is 10-ounces, so a good size for a smoothie. It also looks a lot like a beverage glass, and is easy to drink out of. I like that.
- The blender glass is very easy to clean.
- The bottom of the blender has a rubber pad that helps keep it from moving on the counter while blending.

The Bad:
- Doesn't come with the USB adapter - just the USB cable.
- Doesn't chop frozen fruit very well if the fruit is 1-inch pieces - such as frozen pineapple chunks. It will chop frozen blueberries easily, but it struggles with pieces that are larger.
- If the blender can't chop whatever is in there, it will stop and the red light appears. You have to either remove the glass and scrape down the sides of the glass, or you have to shake the glass to get the contents to move. Pulsing the blender does not help.
- The base of the blender is a little tricky to clean. When you remove the glass, some of the contents might drip into the rim around the blades, so you have to rinse that out carefully without getting the base wet.

The Workaround:
- If using frozen fruit, allow the fruit to slightly thaw before blending. This isn't an ideal workaround when you're running short on time, but it will help.
- Gently shake the blender and tip it upside down and then right side up again while it's turned on. This helps to move the contents of the blender around for more even blending.
- Put frozen fruit or chunky things into the glass first, then add the rest of your smooth ingredients (such as ice cream, yogurt, milk, etc.). By doing this, the blender will blend the smooth things first and the chunkier bits will eventually fall down and get blended - you will have to shake the blender a little to help move those chunky bits down. IF you put the soft items in first, and end with the chunky bits, the blades hit those larger bits first and it has a harder time blending without shutting off.

If you turn on the blender and leave it run while sitting on the counter, it turns itself off after a period of time.

Overall, I do think this is a nice blender and it will continue to get used in our house.
